nodes.name: Frame pacing and play clock
nodes.purpose: Runs one simulation pass per swapped frame, waits two vsyncs between swaps, counts play time on the vsync interrupt and ticks the event countdown.

nodes.name: Player control and locomotion
nodes.purpose: Reads the pad, converts stick input to direction bits, then runs the player state machine for idle, turn in place, walk, run, backstep, quick turn and wall probing.

nodes.name: Aiming, lock-on and gunfire
nodes.purpose: Raises the weapon, picks and cycles lock-on targets, steers vertical aim, sweeps a capsule along the shot line, applies distance-banded damage and handles the first-person scope mode.

nodes.name: Player health, wounds and hit reactions
nodes.purpose: Maps the hit point counter to three wound tiers, drains health while poisoned, applies the stagger reaction with its protected window and drives the death state.

nodes.name: Fixed camera cuts and tracking
nodes.purpose: Chooses a pre-authored camera per floor area, switches with a hysteresis test and aims or slides the camera toward the player with eased steps.

nodes.name: Shared enemy perception and steering
nodes.purpose: Holds the cone-of-sight test, the offset-sight wrapper, the turn-toward-target step and the struggle meter that every enemy class reuses.

nodes.name: Enemy classes
nodes.purpose: Per-class brains for a shambling corpse, a clawed brute, a leaping reptile, a four-legged hound and a giant spider: hit points, sight, approach, attack windows and damage to the player.

nodes.name: Room event script interpreter
nodes.purpose: Executes per-room bytecode scripts: an entry script, a per-frame script, sixteen resumable tasks, banked bit flags and item or weapon queries.

nodes.name: Inventory and item use
nodes.purpose: Stores carried items as packed words, enforces slot capacity and ammo stacking on pickup and applies healing item effects.

nodes.name: Interaction triggers and doors
nodes.purpose: Tests probe points ahead of the player against authored trigger rectangles for doors, stairs, climbs, inspect points and pickups, then plays a data-driven door transition.

cards.name: Two-vsync frame cadence and play clock
cards.summary: The game swaps buffers only after two vsyncs have passed, so every per-update constant in the player and enemy code is a 30 Hz value, while the play clock counts the raw 60 Hz interrupt.
cards.behavior: The swap routine spins until the interrupt counter reaches two, swaps the double buffer, zeroes the counter and then calls the per-frame callback. Every task runs once from the user main, so player, enemy, camera and event code advance once per presented frame. The vsync interrupt only bumps the counter and, while a play-time flag is set, adds one to a play clock that is capped at a very large value, so the clock ticks at 60 per second even though the simulation ticks at 30. The event timer used by timed room events loses two units on each frame callback. When adapting any rate in this library, treat angle steps and speeds as per 30 Hz update.

constants.name: Vsyncs per simulation frame
constants.unit: vsyncs at 60 Hz per frame, giving a 30 Hz update at 30 Hz

constants.name: Play clock cap
constants.unit: vsync ticks at 60 Hz, about 1000 hours

constants.name: Event timer decrement
constants.unit: timer units removed per 30 Hz frame callback

cards.name: Stick to direction bits and turn-rate scalar
cards.summary: Analog sticks past about half deflection become digital direction bits with forward and one lateral side winning ties, and a turn scalar of one (0.8 when badly hurt) scales every turn step except in first-person look, where it follows stick deflection.
cards.behavior: The pad routine turns each stick axis into the same direction bits as the d-pad once deflection passes 63 of 127, then removes the opposite bit so forward beats backward and one lateral direction beats the other. A separate ramp variable grows by 4 per update while a lateral bit is held, saturates at 127 and halves every update when released. In the normal third-person mode that ramp is ignored and the turn scalar is fixed at one, or 0.8 in the worst wound tier. Only in the first-person look mode is the scalar the ramp magnitude divided by 128, again with the 0.8 penalty in the worst tier. Every turn constant in the other cards is multiplied by this scalar.

constants.name: Stick to digital threshold
constants.unit: stick units out of 127 full deflection

constants.name: Digital ramp step
constants.unit: ramp units per update at 30 Hz while a lateral bit is held

cards.name: Tank-style turn rates per gait
cards.summary: Left and right never strafe: they only add a fixed yaw step per update, with a different step for standing, walking, running, backing and aiming.
cards.behavior: The action selector reads the held direction bits and dispatches one gait per update. Standing turns spin the body at the largest step while the turn animation plays forward or in reverse for the two directions. Walking and backing use a smaller step, running uses a slightly larger step than walking, and while the weapon is raised the step drops to the smallest value so aiming stays precise. Every step is a number of degrees multiplied by 182.04445 to get the 16-bit angle word, truncated to an integer after the turn scalar is applied. Forward motion is separate: the body keeps translating along its current yaw while the yaw changes, so curves come from combining forward and turn.

constants.unit: degrees per update at 30 Hz before the turn scalar

constants.name: Degrees to angle words

cards.name: Walk, run, idle and push gaits
cards.summary: Walk and run speed is read per animation frame from motion translation data rather than a constant, run needs forward plus the run button, and a few modifiers slow the body.
cards.behavior: Forward speed each update is looked up from a translation table indexed by the current motion frame, so footfalls move the body and speed varies through the cycle. Wading, flagged by a status bit, multiplies that speed by 0.8, and in one special mode the middle and worst wound tiers multiply it by 0.8 and 0.6. Running starts when the run button is held with forward; releasing the run button drops back to walking while releasing forward drops to idle. Walking into a pushable obstacle counts updates, and after more than five the push gait takes over. A healthy player who stays untouched for more than 300 updates enters an idle animation that ends on any input.

constants.unit: multiplier on per-frame translation speed (at 30 Hz)

constants.name: Worst-tier walk multiplier in the special mode
constants.unit: multiplier on per-frame translation speed (at 30 Hz)

constants.name: Push gait trigger
constants.unit: updates at 30 Hz of walking into an obstacle before the push gait

constants.name: Idle animation delay
constants.unit: updates standing untouched (10 s at 30 Hz)

cards.name: Quick turn by pressing run while backing up
cards.summary: A fresh run press during the backstep spins the player a half circle in eight equal steps at 30 Hz, nearly in place, and drops into a run.
cards.behavior: While in the backstep gait, a newly pressed run button sets the target heading to the current heading plus half a circle and raises an eased-turn flag. Each update the heading moves by the remaining difference divided by a counter that starts at eight and decrements. Because the remainder shrinks in step with the divisor, every step is the same size, one eighth of the half circle (4096 angle words, 22.5 degrees per update at 30 Hz), so the turn is linear, not accelerating, and the heading is forced onto the target when the counter reaches zero. The run gait starts immediately with a long blend, a footstep sound and the wall probe lead extended to its run value. The turn also sets a flag that makes the run gait zero its forward speed, so the player does not run forward during the turn; the body only slides sideways by a small fixed amount each update until the flag clears at the end. Afterward the player keeps running only if forward and run are still held.

constants.name: Half circle offset
constants.unit: angle words; one more word is added, so 32768 = 180 degrees

constants.name: Easing steps
constants.unit: updates at 30 Hz for the heading ease; divisor starts here and decrements

constants.name: Run blend frames
constants.unit: animation blend updates at 30 Hz when entering run from the quick turn

constants.name: Run probe lead
constants.unit: units ahead of the body for wall probing

constants.name: Sideways slide during the turn
constants.unit: units per update at 30 Hz, perpendicular to the target heading, while forward speed is zero

cards.name: Guarded backstep near a frontal enemy
cards.summary: Backing up normally uses one gait, but when a live enemy stands within 30 units inside the forward 75 degree cone the player swaps to a slower retreat gait that keeps facing the threat.
cards.behavior: While backing up in the healthiest wound tier, the code checks every update whether any active enemy is within 30 units horizontally and within 75 degrees of the facing direction, with no wall between them. If so the gait changes to a second retreat gait driven by its own translation table, steered at the walk turn step. While that gait runs, if the enemy leaves the cone or range control returns to the normal backstep, and releasing backward returns to idle. This produces a slow, readable back-away that cannot outrun a close enemy unless the player turns and runs.

constants.name: Retreat steering
constants.unit: degrees per update at 30 Hz before the turn scalar

constants.name: Backstep wall probe lead
constants.unit: units behind the body for wall probing

cards.name: Wall probe lead and body capsule
cards.summary: Walls are tested with a point that leads the body by a smoothed distance, and the body is a 3.5-radius capsule while the hurt volume is a separate 2.5-radius capsule.
cards.behavior: Each gait sets a target probe lead: zero while standing, 2 units when walking, 3 when running and minus 1 when backing up. The live lead eases to its target by half the remaining gap each update. The probe sits that far ahead of the player and 12.5 units above the feet; the wall solver pushes it out of walls, and the resulting offset is applied to the player so sliding along walls falls out for free. A second test then keeps the full body capsule out of walls. A recoil flag, set by heavy weapons, pushes the body backward at its current speed, which halves every update until it is under 0.1. Enemy hits use a separate hurt capsule between the upper body and the root with radius 2.5.

constants.name: Probe lead smoothing
constants.unit: fraction of the remaining gap per update at 30 Hz

cards.name: Raise weapon and lock the nearest visible enemy
cards.summary: Raising the weapon scans all enemies in a full circle, picks the nearest one with a clear line, then eases the body yaw onto it over eight updates.
cards.behavior: When the ready button goes down the player enters a short raise state. The scan passes a half-angle of zero, which the search treats as 180 degrees, so every active and targetable enemy qualifies unless a wall blocks a thin capsule from chest height to the target centre. The nearest qualifying enemy by 3D distance is chosen and marked as locked. The wanted yaw is recomputed from a point 3 units out from the body so the shot line, not the chest, crosses the target. A flag starts the yaw ease: each update the heading moves by the remaining difference divided by a counter that starts at eight. If nothing qualifies the weapon simply rises straight ahead and the body turns at the slow aim rate.

constants.name: Scan half-angle
constants.unit: angle words (180 degrees, used when the argument is zero)

constants.name: Yaw ease steps
constants.unit: updates at 30 Hz for the lock-on turn

constants.name: Muzzle alignment offset
constants.unit: units out from the body used to recompute the yaw

constants.name: Line-of-sight probe radius
constants.unit: units, capsule radius for the wall test

cards.name: Retarget cycling and three-position vertical aim
cards.summary: While aiming, a retarget press jumps to the next-nearest enemy in an 85 degree cone, and aim up or down snaps between level, up and down at plus or minus 45 degrees.
cards.behavior: A fresh retarget press builds a list of qualifying enemies inside an 85 degree half cone with a clear line, sorts it by distance and picks the nearest one not yet visited; when all were visited the marks reset and it wraps to the nearest (or the second nearest if the nearest is the current target). The yaw ease for a retarget is four updates instead of eight. Holding aim-up or aim-down together with the ready button switches among three aim states, and the weapon pitch eases to the goal by a quarter of the gap each update; the goals are level, plus 45 degrees and minus 45 degrees. Steering stays available at the aim turn rate so the player can sweep between targets. Single-position weapons skip the pitch change.

constants.name: Pitch easing divisor
constants.unit: gap divided by 4 per update at 30 Hz

cards.name: Shot as a widening capsule sweep
cards.summary: A shot is a 200-unit line from 11 units above the feet; the hit capsule starts 2 units wide and widens with distance by a capped amount, which acts as built-in aim assistance.
cards.behavior: On firing, the shot starts slightly ahead of the player at 11 units above the ground and runs along the weapon yaw and pitch for the weapon length. The sweep tests every active enemy against a capsule whose radius is the weapon base radius plus a growth term, the distance along the line times a growth factor. Only the growth term is capped; the base radius is added after the cap. For the sample weapon row the radius therefore tops out at 2 plus 4, which is 6 units. When aiming up or down the growth factor is doubled and the growth cap multiplied by 1.2 (to 4.8, so 6.8 units at most) so slanted shots forgive more. Other weapon rows use other numbers, for example growth 0.2 with a cap of 1.0, or growth 0.3 with a cap of 40. Enemies behind the shooter are skipped, walls shorten the line and add a margin, and the nearest enemy hit takes the damage. Because the capsule widens with range, a far target is easier to hit than its model width suggests.

constants.name: Base hit radius, sample weapon row
Radius growth per unit of range, sample weapon row
constants.unit: units of radius per unit of distance

constants.name: Radius growth cap, sample weapon row
constants.unit: units added on top of the base radius, so the capsule is at most 6.0 wide

constants.name: Angled-aim growth cap multiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on the radius growth cap (not the whole radius) when aimed up or down

cards.name: Distance-banded damage tables per enemy and weapon
cards.summary: Damage is read from three tables indexed by enemy class and weapon slot, selected by whether the hit is under 15 units, under 40 units or farther.
cards.behavior: After the capsule sweep finds the nearest enemy, the damaged joint is the one closest to the impact point unless the weapon is flagged to use the swept joint. The distance from the muzzle to the impact picks the near, mid or far table, and the pick also sets a flag bit that the enemy brain can read. The value is added to that joint damage counter. Each enemy brain later sums its joint counters into total damage and subtracts that from its hit points. Weapon slots 18 and 20 hold 999 in every band, so they act as instant kills. For one sample enemy row and weapon slot 3 the values fall from 18 up close to 15 mid-range and 12 far away.

constants.name: Near damage, sample enemy row, weapon slot 3
Mid damage, sample enemy row, weapon slot 3
Far damage, sample enemy row, weapon slot 3

cards.name: Fire gate, dry fire and recoil push
cards.summary: A shot needs the weapon raised, ammo and a fresh fire press (an empty weapon clicks or reloads), and heavy weapons shove the shooter backward with a velocity that halves each update.
cards.behavior: While the weapon is raised, a shot fires when the ready button and the fire button are both held, the per-press latch is clear, the weapon is ready again and ammo remains. Firing sets the latch and it clears only when the fire button is released, so each shot needs a fresh press. With no ammo the fire press must be a fresh edge; it plays a dry-fire click, or starts a reload if spare ammunition exists. Some weapons push the shooter: the initial backward speed depends on the character and weapon, then it is multiplied by one half every update until it is under 0.1 units per update. A new shot cannot start until the ready-again flag, raised near the end of the firing animation, comes back, which sets the rate of fire.

constants.name: Recoil speed, first character
constants.unit: units per update at 30 Hz, halves each update

constants.name: Recoil speed, second character
constants.unit: units per update at 30 Hz, halves each update

constants.name: Heavy weapon recoil, first character
constants.unit: units per update at 30 Hz, halves each update

cards.name: First-person scope aim with zoom and recoil wobble
cards.summary: A scope weapon switches to a free-aim first-person view with a stick dead zone, zoom between 65 and 20 degrees of field of view, and a decaying wobble after each shot.
cards.behavior: In scope mode the stick moves yaw and pitch at four angle words per stick unit beyond a dead zone of 48, and digital buttons use the ramped value instead. Pitch is clamped to plus or minus 45 degrees. Holding the zoom button narrows the field of view from 65 to 20 degrees. The weapon may fire after the first six updates. The shot starts from the scope bone and travels along the aim angles, then pitch wobbles around its starting value for thirty updates with amplitude 2048 reduced by 64 each step and a sine phase that advances about 10.5 degrees per update. Releasing the ready button after the settle delay leaves scope mode.

constants.name: Aim gain
constants.unit: angle words per stick unit per update at 30 Hz

cards.name: Fixed camera selection with boundary hysteresis
cards.summary: Each floor area maps to an authored camera, and the camera switches only when the player and all four one-unit neighbours lie outside the current area.
cards.behavior: Every update the code finds which authored camera area contains the player ground point on the current floor. If it differs from the current camera it probes four points one unit north, south, west and east of the player, and hands over to the new camera only if none of them still falls in the current area. That hysteresis stops flicker when the player straddles a boundary. When the player is climbing or in some transitions the test uses the root bone position instead of the ground point. The previous camera is remembered for fades and hidden-object lists, and a fresh room load picks the camera directly without the check.

constants.name: Probe offset
constants.unit: units on each axis around the player

cards.name: Eased aim and slide inside a fixed camera
cards.summary: Inside one cut the camera position slides in proportion to where the player stands in the area, and its aim eases toward the player by a per-camera factor.
cards.behavior: The tracked player point eases halfway toward the smoothed player position each update, and its height is the floor height plus a per-camera offset. Camera position along the width and depth axes is an authored anchor plus the player offset scaled by authored percentages, so a camera drifts as the player walks. Aim angles ease by a per-camera percentage of the angle gap each update, and a camera can clamp its look range to limit pan and tilt. Position eases by an authored fraction of the gap each update. Right after a cut that sets the transition flag, an alternate mode runs for one plus an authored count of updates: a counter starts at zero and each update the position moves by that counter times one over one plus the count of the remaining gap, so the pull ramps up from nothing and the mode ends when the counter reaches the count plus one. The default camera distance is 256 and the default perspective is 8192 angle words.

constants.name: Tracked point easing
constants.unit: fraction of the gap per update at 30 Hz

constants.name: Authored percent scale
constants.unit: multiplier converting stored percent values to fractions

constants.name: Alternate easing numerator
constants.unit: divided by one plus an authored count, then multiplied by a transition counter that rises by 1 each update at 30 Hz

cards.name: Hit points, wound tiers and poison drain
cards.summary: The player has 160 hit points (320 in the alternate mode); tiers at 120 and 30 change the walk animations and turn speed, and poison removes one point every 31 updates.
cards.behavior: Health starts at 160, or 320 in one alternate game mode. A tier check runs inside the gait states: at 120 or more the tier is zero unless a poison status is set, from 30 to 119 it is one, and below 30 it is two. A tier change swaps the animation set and keeps the blend frame, and the worst tier adds a turn penalty of 0.8. While a damage-over-time status mask is set, a counter adds one per update, and when it passes 30 it resets and takes one hit point if hit points are above zero. Health below zero starts the death state unless a death-handled flag is already set.

constants.name: Poison drain interval
constants.unit: updates at 30 Hz counted before 1 hit point is lost (31 updates per point)

cards.name: Stagger reaction with built-in invulnerability
cards.summary: A successful enemy hit sets a hit flag and starts a stagger animation; the flag makes every other enemy attack test bail out until the animation ends.
cards.behavior: Every enemy attack first checks that the player hit flag is clear, then tests a sphere against the player capsule inside its animation window. A hit sets the flag, subtracts the damage, picks a front or back stagger from the attacker and player headings and switches the player to the damage state. That state clears the aiming flags, plays the stagger with a short blend, speaks a voice line and moves the player along a table-driven recoil. When the animation reaches its last frame it clears the flag and returns to normal control. Because every attack tests the flag first, the stagger length is also the invulnerable window.

cards.name: Grab struggle by button mashing
cards.summary: While an enemy holds the player, each fresh press shortens the grab countdown: a direction press removes four extra units and an action press three, on top of one per update.
cards.behavior: Grabs run a countdown that drops by one every update. The shared struggle function adds four when any direction was newly pressed this update and three more when any face or shoulder button was newly pressed, so alternating both gives up to eight units per update. Held buttons do nothing because only new edges count. Damage is dealt at fixed animation frames independent of the countdown, so a quick escape skips the later hits. The shambling class starts the countdown at 60 for its heavy bite; its lighter hold ignores the countdown and ends with its animation.

constants.name: Direction press bonus
constants.unit: countdown units per update at 30 Hz when a direction edge occurred

constants.name: Action press bonus
constants.unit: countdown units per update at 30 Hz when an action button edge occurred

constants.name: Light bite damage base
constants.unit: hit points plus the variant bonus; this lighter hold ends with its animation, not the countdown

cards.name: Sight cones with timed memory
cards.summary: Enemies see the player only inside a facing cone with no distance limit, then keep tracking for a class-specific time after the player leaves the cone.
cards.behavior: The shared sight test compares the angle between an enemy facing and the direction to the player with a half-angle, the limit on either side of the facing, so each stored angle gives a cone twice as wide; a half-angle of zero means 180 degrees each side, which is all around the enemy. The shambling class tests every update with an 80 or 60 degree half-angle (a 160 or 120 degree cone) depending on variant and holds a sighting until the 31-update cycle counter reaches its last value without the player in view. The code also sets a 15-update afterglow counter for the alert flag, but that countdown is dead: the counter is an unsigned byte, so the check for a negative value never succeeds and the flag is cleared only by other code paths. The same dead countdown appears in the brute code. The clawed brute uses a 100 degree half-angle (a 200 degree cone) with the same cycle. The hound tests only during the first four updates of each sixteen-update cycle with the same 100 degree half-angle. The leaping reptile needs a vertical gap under 30 units and an unobstructed ray at 15 units height, uses a 120 degree half-angle (a 240 degree cone) and forgets after 90 updates.

constants.unit: angle words, half-angle (80 degrees each side, 160 degree cone)

constants.name: Shambling cone half-angle, narrow variant
constants.unit: angle words, half-angle (60 degrees each side, 120 degree cone)

constants.unit: updates at 30 Hz intended; the unsigned counter never goes negative, so it has no effect

constants.name: Brute cone half-angle
constants.unit: angle words, half-angle 18204 (100 degrees each side, 200 degree cone)

constants.name: Hound cone half-angle
constants.unit: angle words, half-angle (100 degrees each side, 200 degree cone)

constants.name: Reptile cone half-angle
constants.unit: angle words, half-angle (120 degrees each side, 240 degree cone)

cards.name: Fixed-step turn toward a target
cards.summary: Enemies rotate toward their goal by a fixed angle step per update at 30 Hz that snaps when the gap is within one step either side, with each class and state choosing its own step.
cards.behavior: The steering helper takes a goal point and a signed step. It computes the heading to the goal and the difference to the current heading. The difference is shifted by one step and wrapped to a half-open window; if the result is below twice the step, which means the gap is no more than one step either way, the heading is set exactly to the goal; otherwise the heading moves one step in the shorter direction. A negative step turns away, which retreat states use. The shambling class steps 256 angle words (about 1.4 degrees) per update while approaching and 512 (about 2.8 degrees) once it is within about 20 units, so it turns slowly and can be circled. The hound steps 1152 (about 6.3 degrees) when sprinting.

constants.name: Shambling approach step
constants.unit: angle words per update at 30 Hz (1.4 degrees)

constants.name: Shambling close step
constants.unit: angle words per update at 30 Hz (2.8 degrees)

constants.name: Hound sprint step
constants.unit: angle words per update at 30 Hz (6.3 degrees)

cards.name: Shambling corpse class: variant stats, chase gates and grab
cards.summary: A random-hit-point walker that starts chasing when sighted inside its attack distance, speeds up inside 20 units and gives up beyond a per-variant distance.
cards.behavior: Hit points are drawn at random from a sixteen-entry table, 60 to 120 normally and 20 to 60 in the alternate mode, then raised by a per-variant percentage. Each variant also defines the sight angle, an attack-start distance of 20 to 50 units and a give-up distance of 50 to 100. While wandering, a sighted player inside the attack distance starts the chase, and within 15 units the walker pauses instead of closing further. During the chase, inside 20 units (25 if flagged) the gait speeds up with a wider turn step, and it relaxes again after the player stays beyond 25 (30) for a random 30 to 90 updates. Beyond the give-up distance, or with the player no longer sighted, it returns to wandering when the current step cycle ends. The grab deals damage twice, at fixed animation frames, each equal to the variant bonus plus 10.

constants.name: Lowest hit point entry, normal mode
Highest hit point entry, normal mode
Grab damage base
constants.unit: hit points per grab tick, plus the variant bonus

constants.name: First grab damage frame
constants.unit: animation frame (the second tick is at frame 60)

cards.name: Clawed brute: range-gated attack selector
cards.summary: The brute chooses among four attacks with range, health and random gates, and hits with a sphere that is active only on a few animation frames.
cards.behavior: Hit points are drawn from a sixteen-entry table, 105 to 150 normally and 75 to 120 in the alternate mode. Each update the brain tests four attacks in order: an enraged long reach attack when the brute has under 75 hit points and the player under 80, the plain reach attack, a close sweep under 13 units, and a leap at a player standing up to 10 units higher at 14 to 50 units away with a one-in-32 chance per update (one-in-8 while a player movement flag is set). The reach attacks need a distance above 17 and under 20 units, a clear line and the player roughly in front. The sweep sphere has radius 3, is tested only on frames 10 to 15 and does 20 damage; the grab connects at frame 15 for 30; a grab attempt blocked by a wall hits for 10 instead. Each hit sets the player hit flag, so attacks do not chain.

constants.name: Lowest hit point entry, normal mode
Highest hit point entry, normal mode

cards.name: Leaping reptile: poison claws and low-health finisher
cards.summary: The reptile hits in short frame windows, one variant can poison with a 40 percent chance, and a weakened reptile may try a neck finisher when the player is nearly dead.
cards.behavior: Hit points come from a sixteen-entry table, 120 to 165 normally and 45 to 75 in the alternate mode. The claw hit lands only when a sphere of radius 5 on the claw joint overlaps the player during animation frames 14 to 17 and removes 20; a heavier slash from frame 12 onward removes 50. For one model variant each hit has a 40 percent chance to set the poison status. When the player hit points are below 100 (110 for the other characters), the reptile is within 30 units and faces the player within about 20 degrees, it may start the neck finisher, but only if its own hit points are below 60: the finisher stays armed with 50 percent chance under 30 hit points and 25 percent between 30 and 59. Otherwise a claw swipe window can launch the claw attack with 50 percent chance, or 75 percent when the player is at 120 hit points or less.

constants.name: Lowest hit point entry, normal mode
Highest hit point entry, normal mode
Poison chance
constants.unit: probability per hit for the poison variant

constants.name: Finisher player threshold
constants.unit: player hit points, first character (110 for the others)

cards.name: Four-legged hound: accelerating sprint and arc leap
cards.summary: The hound starts a sprint slowly, adds 0.1 units per update up to 1.2, and from 20 units away leaps in an arc with distance-gated bite damage.
cards.behavior: Hit points come from a table of 60 to 120 normally and 30 to 75 in the alternate mode. In the sprint state the speed starts at 0.08 and grows by 0.1 per update until it reaches 1.2, while the hound turns toward the target at 1152 angle words per update. When the player is within 20 units but beyond 11 and the hound faces within about 6 degrees with a clear line, it starts the leap: an 11-update windup at 0.4 units per update, then a launch at 1.9 units per update with an initial vertical velocity of 2.2 upward that loses 0.28 each update at 30 Hz, which gives a parabolic arc. A sphere of radius 1.2 on the head is tested; a hit from frame 13 on removes 12 hit points and an earlier one removes 6. Inside 11 units the hound does a close attack instead.

constants.name: Lowest hit point entry, normal mode
Highest hit point entry, normal mode
Sprint acceleration
constants.unit: units per update at 30 Hz, added each update

constants.name: Leap gravity step
constants.unit: units per update subtracted from the vertical velocity each update at 30 Hz (a downward pull of 0.28 units per update squared)

cards.name: Giant spider: two health pools and flinch thresholds
cards.summary: The spider has a main health pool and a smaller weak-point pool; weak-side hits drain only the weak pool, and it flinches only when one update deals at least 30 damage.
cards.behavior: Each spider rolls a main pool of 130 to 180 and a weak pool of 50 to 90 in normal mode (90 to 150 and 30 to 70 in the alternate mode). A dot product of the incoming shot direction against a stored orientation vector decides whether a hit counts as weak-side. A weak-side hit subtracts damage from only the weak pool; any other hit subtracts from the main pool and, when a guard flag and the aim flag allow it, from the weak pool too. When the weak pool goes below zero certain weapon classes force a collapse after a minimum number of hits. Flinching depends on total damage in one update: under 30 nothing happens, 30 to 49 gives a small flinch and 50 or more a large one. The held bite removes 12 hit points, or 5 once a chain counter passes 30.

cards.name: Room event script interpreter with resumable tasks
cards.summary: Each room runs a bytecode script on entry and another every frame, using a 256-entry opcode table, sixteen resumable tasks and bit flags kept in banked arrays.
cards.behavior: On room entry the init routine runs the entry script, then enables the scheduler for one pass; every frame afterward the second script runs and the scheduler runs again, doing work only while its enable flag is set. An opcode handler returns nonzero to continue with the next opcode and zero to stop for the frame. Long-running work lives in up to sixteen tasks: each active task keeps a resume pointer and executes opcodes until one yields, then the pointer is saved for the next frame. A flag is addressed by a bank number and a ten-bit index that picks a 32-bit word and a bit; conditions compare one flag with a wanted value. If and else use a small stack of resume pointers. Item opcodes search the packed inventory, query the equipped weapon and delete an item by shifting later slots down.

cards.name: Slot-limited inventory with two-slot items and ammo stacks
cards.summary: Pickups use eight slots (ten after an expansion); large items cost two slots and ammunition stacks to 999 with overflow carried to the next stack.
cards.behavior: Each item is one packed word with the item id in bits 16 to 23 and the count in the low bits. On pickup the code walks the carried slots, subtracting one free slot for each item and two for items flagged as large. If the picked item is ammunition and a stack of the same id is below 999 it adds the pickup amount, carries any amount beyond 999 to the next matching stack, and needs no free slot once everything fits. When enough room exists the pickup moves to a confirm prompt; otherwise the no-room path runs. Starting capacity is 8, raised to 10 by an expansion flag.

cards.name: Healing items and the hit point cap
cards.summary: Healing items add 50 or 100 hit points (double in the alternate mode) or restore fully, hit points are clamped at the cap, and a cure flag clears poison.
cards.behavior: The used item index selects a cure code: its low nibble gives the heal size and its high nibble the poison cure. Size one adds 50 hit points, size two adds 100, and sizes three and four restore to the maximum of 160. In the alternate mode these become 100, 200 and 320. The result is clamped to the cap. A cure code removes the poison status. The routine reports whether the item was used; with nothing to heal or cure it shows a message instead. Afterward the status screen recomputes its wound colour with breaks at 120, 60 and 30.

cards.name: Interaction triggers from probe points and rectangles
cards.summary: Doors, stairs, climbs, inspect points and pickups are rectangles on a floor; five probe points ahead of the player test them and the action button starts the matching action.
cards.behavior: When the action button is newly pressed and the player is in a free state, the code builds five probe points in front of the player: two measured from the smoothed wall probe at 1.5 and 3 units plus its shortfall, and three from the body root at 0.75, 2 and 4.5 units. Each trigger rectangle has a type that selects the probe it uses: door, stairs, climb, inspect or item pickup. Door, inspect and pickup triggers also reject the press when the player heading falls in a quadrant blocked by their attribute bits. A door freezes the player and stores destination stage, room and position numbers for the transition. Stairs start a climb animation selected by direction and size, and a climb needs the point 6 units ahead to lie inside its rectangle with no wall in front.

constants.name: Door heading offset
constants.unit: angle words (45 degrees) added before the quadrant test

cards.name: Data-driven door transition playback
cards.summary: A door plays as a short scripted scene made of fade, camera, door-swing, light and rumble procedures that tick together, with a speed mode that repeats the tick to fast-forward.
cards.behavior: On a door trigger the transition loads one parameter block per door type. Each block selects up to five procedures: a fade, a view, a door animation, a light change and a rumble. Every frame the controller runs each active procedure once, repeats the whole pass for fast speed modes, increments a door time counter and plays sounds on bits the procedures raise. Door animation procedures drive angular speed through authored wait, accelerate and decelerate steps. The scene uses a near clip of minus 2 and a far clip of minus 20000 by default, with a small override table for specific views, an aspect scale of 1.174, and a perspective of 12743 angle words, about 70 degrees.
